rules.instruction: When the description states that a send step is addressed to a team or recipient that it names explicitly, for example in an example that says which named team receives or makes which item: Label the send task with the recipient name and the item as the description states them, rather than with a generic group term such as 'part teams' or 'partners'. Keep the named recipient's identity visible in the label so that the task reads as the same delivery the description gives.
rules.situation: the description states that a send step is addressed to a team or recipient that it names explicitly, for example in an example that says which named team receives or makes which item

rules.instruction: When the description says that a record is created or updated while an activity is carried out, and that this record is then sent to one or more parties: Model the creation or update of the record as its own user task placed on the flow after the activity that produces the information and before the send task that transmits the record. Do not fold the creation into the activity itself or leave the send task without a producing step before it. Connect the send task to any parties that receive the record.
rules.situation: the description says that a record is created or updated while an activity is carried out, and that this record is then sent to one or more parties

rules.instruction: When the description says the process offers a set of options or a request to an external party, such as a customer, and that party then returns its choices before the process can continue: Model the offer as a sendTask, and model the returned choices as a receiveTask placed immediately after it in the main sequence and before any task that works on those choices. Do not model the returned choices as a new start event, because the process has already begun, and do not let the send step stand in for the return.
rules.situation: the description says the process offers a set of options or a request to an external party, such as a customer, and that party then returns its choices before the process can continue

rules.instruction: When the description says that the recipient of a delivered item has to confirm receipt before the process can continue: After the activity that delivers the item, model the awaited confirmation from the recipient as an intermediate message catch event that gates the subsequent flow, placed in the sequence after the delivery activity. Do not model the wait as a task, and do not omit it.
rules.situation: the description says that the recipient of a delivered item has to confirm receipt before the process can continue
